title: Silent Signals, Loud Impact: LLMs for Word-Sense Disambiguation of Coded Dog Whistles
measurement_description: The paper measures the ability of Large Language Models to perform word-sense disambiguation on 'dog whistles'—a form of coded communication. In relation to religion, this includes the detection and disambiguation of Islamophobic and antisemitic dog whistles from standard language in both formal (U.S. Congressional Records) and informal (Reddit) contexts.
findings: The study successfully created the 'Silent Signals' dataset, the largest dataset of disambiguated dog whistles, which includes significant categories for Islamophobic and antisemitic coded language. For example, the term 'terrorist' was identified as an Islamophobic dog whistle implying that 'Muslim people on a whole are a threat'. The distribution of these religious dog whistles was analyzed over time and across formal (political speeches) and informal (social media) contexts. While LLMs like GPT-4 could be used to create the dataset with high precision, their overall reliability on the automatic resolution task remains a challenge.
